intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime merchants and discover the heart of Tokyo's culinary culture in one of the world's most famous food markets.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture hub. Visit multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, explore retro game shops, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Experience the epicenter of Japanese tech culture and otaku subculture firsthand.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, and stroll through the historic Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and immerse yourself in centuries of Edo-period culture and architecture.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most immersive digital art installations where technology and creativity merge seamlessly. Walk through infinite mirror rooms, interactive light forests, and flowing digital waterfalls. A perfect fusion of Tokyo's tech innovation and artistic culture that redefines the museum experience.

experiences.name: Ramen and Izakaya Night Tour in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the atmospheric Golden Gai alleyways and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku for an authentic evening of local dining. Slurp handcrafted ramen, share yakitori skewers, and sip sake at tiny izakayas packed with locals. A quintessential Tokyo night food experience full of flavor and character.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly airport limousine bus or train to Tsukiji (~900–1,300 JPY). Check in to your Tsukiji boutique stay, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings. Browse the small street food stalls and fish-related shops along Shin-Ohashi-dori.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tsukiji Outer Market evening vendors still open late afternoon. Head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens entrance area for a sunset stroll along the waterfront (free from outside). Grab dinner at one of the affordable Tsukiji Outer Market eateries — fresh sushi sets, tamagoyaki, and grilled seafood skewers are iconic here.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Airport meal or convenience store onigiri/bento at 7-Eleven or FamilyMart (~500 JPY)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market stalls — fresh sushi set or grilled scallops and tamagoyaki (~800–1,200 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, subways, and buses in Tokyo and saves money vs. buying individual tickets. Rest early to beat jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its freshest (6:00–8:00 AM). Try a breakfast of fresh tuna sashimi don (tuna rice bowl) or tamagoyaki sandwich from the market vendors. Walk 10 minutes to Hamarikyu Gardens (300 JPY entry) — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, teahouse, and seasonal cherry blossom remnants in mid-April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line from Tsukiji Station to Akihabara (~20 min, ~200 JPY). Spend the afternoon immersed in Tokyo's legendary tech and anime culture. Browse multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera, explore retro game shops, and visit the free floors of Akihabara UDX building for tech exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and evening exploration. Visit a maid café for a unique cultural experience (~500–1,000 JPY for a drink and performance). Browse the illuminated arcades and Gundam/anime figure shops after dark. Return to Tsukiji via Hibiya Line.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — tamagoyaki sandwich or mini tuna don (~500–800 JPY)
meals.lunch: Akihabara — Curry House CoCo Ichibanya or a ramen shop near Electric Town (~700–1,000 JPY)
meals.dinner: Akihabara — Yoshinoya gyudon (beef bowl) or a conveyor-belt sushi Kura Sushi (~600–1,000 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is the heart of Tokyo's tech and otaku culture — perfect for your interests. Free WiFi is available in most electronics stores. Weekday afternoons are less crowded than weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Toei Asakusa Line from Higashi-Ginza (near Tsukiji) to Asakusa (~15 min, ~180 JPY). Visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple — free entry. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to beat crowds. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs and snacks like ningyo-yaki and kaminari-okoshi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa neighborhood on foot — visit Asakusa Shrine, walk along the Sumida River, and admire the view of the Tokyo Skytree (you can see it for free from the riverbank). Cross to Kappabashi 'Kitchen Town' (10-min walk) — a fascinating street of restaurant supply shops selling plastic food models, knives, and cookware, all free to browse.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Ginza Line from Asakusa to Ueno (~5 min, ~170 JPY). Explore Ueno Park at dusk — free to enter and beautiful in April with late cherry blossoms. Visit Ameyoko Market, a lively outdoor market street with cheap street food, clothing, and snacks. Have dinner at one of Ameyoko's affordable izakayas.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa — Asakusa Imahan convenience store or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten (coffee shop) (~400–700 JPY)
meals.lunch: Asakusa Nakamise-dori snacks — ningyo-yaki, melonpan, and soy sauce crackers (~500 JPY)
meals.dinner: Ueno Ameyoko Market — yakitori skewers, gyoza, or an izakaya set meal (~800–1,200 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and most atmospheric at dawn or dusk. Kappabashi is closed Sundays — good you're visiting Friday. Ameyoko is lively on weekday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Shibuya via Tokyo Metro (~25 min from Tsukiji, ~220 JPY). Start at the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — arrive by 9 AM to see it in action. Visit the free Shibuya Sky observation deck alternative: the free rooftop of Shibuya Hikarie building (8th floor Sky Lobby is free). Walk to Shibuya 109 and the surrounding youth fashion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes north to Harajuku. Explore Takeshita Street for quirky street fashion, crepes, and pop culture. Then walk through the tranquil Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) set in a forested park — a peaceful contrast to the busy streets. Stroll the wide Omotesando boulevard and window-shop the architecture (free to look!).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya for evening. Visit the free Shibuya Stream rooftop area. Have dinner in Shibuya's Dogenzaka area — many affordable ramen, gyoza, and yakiniku spots. Experience the Shibuya Scramble Crossing lit up at night before heading back to Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near Tsukiji hotel — onigiri, hot coffee, and a boiled egg (~350 JPY)
meals.lunch: Harajuku Takeshita Street — rainbow crepe and takoyaki (~600–800 JPY)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — Ichiran Ramen (solo dining booths, iconic experience) (~980 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Takeshita Street and Shibuya will be very crowded — go early. Meiji Jingu is a peaceful escape and free. Ichiran Ramen in Shibuya is a Tokyo must-do that fits the budget well.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic artificial island, via the free Yurikamome Line scenic monorail from Shimbashi (~20 min, ~330 JPY one way). See the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free, outdoors). Walk the Odaiba seaside promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the city skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore teamLab Borderless digital art museum in Odaiba (book in advance, ~3,200 JPY — worth the splurge for tech/culture lovers). If budget is very tight, visit the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza shopping mall and its Gundam Base Tokyo exhibit instead. Walk to Palette Town area and browse the free Venus Fort shopping mall architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via Yurikamome to Shimbashi, then walk or take Metro to Ginza (~5 min from Tsukiji). Window-shop the luxury Ginza district for free — the architecture and street atmosphere are spectacular at night. Have a budget dinner in the backstreets behind Ginza's main boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Tsukiji Outer Market morning snack (~500 JPY)
meals.lunch: Odaiba — Decks Tokyo Beach food court, ramen or udon (~800–1,000 JPY)
meals.dinner: Ginza backstreets — soba noodle shop or standing sushi bar (~700–1,000 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless is a splurge but aligns perfectly with your tech and culture interests — book tickets online in advance to save time. The Gundam statue at DiverCity is completely free and impressive. Odaiba has great free waterfront views.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Tokyo Metro to Shinjuku (~25 min from Tsukiji, ~220 JPY). Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (open from 9 AM, free) for panoramic 360-degree views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding Nishi-Shinjuku skyscraper district on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to East Shinjuku — explore Kabukicho entertainment district by day (safe and interesting to walk through). Visit the free Hanazono Shrine tucked behind the neon signs. Browse Shinjuku's massive Yodobashi Akiba-style electronics multi-floor store. Walk through Shinjuku Golden Gai — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars (best visited evening but fascinating by day too).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku Golden Gai at night — tiny atmospheric bars with 500–800 JPY drinks and unique themes. Have dinner in Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls with smoky, authentic atmosphere (~1,000–1,500 JPY for skewers and beer). Return to Tsukiji via Metro.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku — Matsuya fast food breakfast set or convenience store (~350–500 JPY)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku — Keika Kumamoto Ramen, a classic budget ramen institution (~750 JPY)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — yakitori skewers, grilled offal, cold beer (~1,000–1,500 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free — one of the best views in the city. Golden Gai bars have a small cover charge (500–1,000 JPY) but are a unique cultural experience. Omoide Yokocho is cash only.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko via the budget JR Pass or Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (~2 hours, ~1,360 JPY one way on Tobu Limited Express). Visit the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex (1,300 JPY entry) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with stunning gilded architecture surrounded by cedar forests. Arrive by 10 AM to beat tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Rinno-ji Temple (included in combined ticket) and the serene Shinkyo Sacred Bridge area. Hike the short trail to Kegon Waterfall viewpoint (~550 JPY for elevator, or free from the top overlook). Enjoy the mountain air and forested scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 18:00–19:00. Have a relaxed dinner near Tsukiji or pick up a bento from a convenience store. Rest early after a full day trip.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departure (~350 JPY)
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine set meal, a local Nikko specialty (~1,000–1,500 JPY)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — convenience store bento or simple udon shop (~600–800 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Buy the Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited Tobu line travel to Nikko plus discounts on attractions (~2,670 JPY for 2 days) — better value than single tickets. April is beautiful in Nikko with spring foliage. Start early to maximize time.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Yanaka neighborhood — one of Tokyo's most preserved old-town shitamachi (downtown) districts, free to walk. Stroll Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts, snacks, and local life. Visit Yanaka Cemetery for a peaceful walk among old cherry trees and historic graves (free, not morbid — very atmospheric).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a smaller, less-touristy version of Kyoto's Fushimi Inari with a tunnel of torii gates. Then head to Ueno via a 15-minute walk. Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno Park (~1,000 JPY) — Japan's largest museum covering 2,000 years of Japanese art and culture, perfectly aligned with your cultural interests.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Ueno Park at dusk. Take the Metro back toward Tsukiji and stop at Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic commercial heart. Walk across the famous Nihonbashi Bridge (free) and admire the old merchant district architecture. Have dinner at a local tonkatsu or tempura restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka — traditional Japanese breakfast at a local kissaten or fresh bread from Yanaka bakery (~400–600 JPY)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza — menchi katsu (fried minced meat cutlet) street snack and croquettes (~400–600 JPY)
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi area — tonkatsu set meal at Maisen or a local teishoku restaurant (~900–1,200 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of Tokyo's most authentic neighborhoods and almost entirely free to explore. The Tokyo National Museum has free entry on certain days — check their website. Nezu Shrine is far less crowded than Fushimi Inari in Kyoto.

day_by_day.morning: Take the JR Chuo Line to Koenji (~30 min, ~200 JPY) — a bohemian, counter-culture neighborhood beloved by Tokyo locals. Browse the incredible second-hand clothing shops and vintage record stores along Koenji's covered shopping arcades. Visit Koenji Hikawa Shrine, a quiet neighborhood shrine with a beautiful atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Nakameguro (~20 min by Metro). Walk along the Meguro River canal — lined with cherry trees (late blooms possible in mid-April) and independent cafés, boutiques, and galleries. Browse the stylish shops and street art. Visit the free Daikanyama area nearby for Tokyo's most aesthetically pleasing street architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in the Nakameguro/Daikanyama area for dinner — many affordable but stylish restaurants. Take the Tokyu Toyoko Line to Shibuya then Metro back to Tsukiji. Alternatively, stop at a standing bar (tachinomi) in Nakameguro for an evening drink (~500–600 JPY per drink).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Tsukiji market snack (~400 JPY)
meals.lunch: Koenji — local curry shop or a soba restaurant (~700–900 JPY)
meals.dinner: Nakameguro — ramen shop along the canal or a casual Italian-Japanese fusion café (~900–1,200 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Koenji is a hidden gem for vintage shopping and local culture — very different from tourist Tokyo. Nakameguro is Instagram-famous but genuinely beautiful and free to walk. Both neighborhoods reflect Tokyo's diverse subcultures.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shiodome and the Caretta Shiodome mall (free to enter, 46th floor observation area free) — just 10 minutes walk from Tsukiji. Explore the Panasonic Museum Shiodome (free entry) for an interesting look at Japanese tech and design history. Walk along the Shiodome waterfront and the scenic Hamarikyu Gardens outer paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Ikebukuro (~30 min, ~220 JPY). Visit Sunshine City — a massive complex with a free shopping mall, the Pokémon Center (free to browse), and Namco Namja Town amusement park (free entry, pay per attraction). Explore the Ikebukuro Bic Camera — even larger than Akihabara's and great for tech browsing. Visit the free Ikebukuro Nishiguchi Park.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ikebukuro's lively evening atmosphere — it's Tokyo's second major hub after Shinjuku and less touristy. Visit the Animate flagship store (world's largest anime merchandise store, free to browse). Have dinner at one of Ikebukuro's excellent ramen shops — the area is famous for tsukemen (dipping ramen).

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh fish breakfast or onigiri (~500 JPY)
meals.lunch: Ikebukuro — Namja Town gyoza stadium (various gyoza styles from across Japan, ~800–1,000 JPY)
meals.dinner: Ikebukuro — Fuunji or Rokurinsha tsukemen (dipping ramen) (~900–1,100 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Ikebukuro is a great alternative to Akihabara for anime and tech culture — less crowded and equally interesting. Namja Town's Gyoza Stadium is a fun and affordable food experience. Friday evenings are lively here.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura via JR Yokosuka Line from Shimbashi (~1 hour, ~940 JPY one way). Visit the iconic Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — 400 JPY entry for one of Japan's most famous landmarks. Walk the surrounding temple grounds and climb inside the Buddha statue for an extra 20 JPY.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills to Zeniarai Benzaiten Shrine — a cave shrine where you wash money to multiply it (free entry). Continue to Hase-dera Temple (~400 JPY) for beautiful hydrangea gardens and ocean views over Kamakura. Walk Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 18:00. Stop at Shimbashi for dinner — Shimbashi is a salaryman district famous for affordable izakayas and yakitori under the train tracks. Have a lively Friday/Saturday evening dinner surrounded by Tokyo office workers unwinding.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departure or at Shimbashi Station (~350 JPY)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — Komachi-dori street food: shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a Kamakura specialty (~800–1,000 JPY)
meals.dinner: Shimbashi — izakaya under the train tracks: yakitori, edamame, cold beer (~1,000–1,500 JPY)

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is one of the best day trips from Tokyo for culture and nature. Buy a JR day pass if doing multiple stops. The Daibutsu Hiking Trail takes about 1.5 hours — wear comfortable shoes. April weather in Kamakura is typically mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (~600 JPY, often discounted) — an extraordinary museum covering 400 years of Tokyo's history from Edo period to modern times, directly relevant to your cultural interests. Walk to the nearby Ryogoku Kokugikan sumo arena — even if no tournament is on, the exterior and the Sumo Museum inside (free) are worth visiting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the Sumida River to explore Kiyosumi-Shirakawa — Tokyo's hippest specialty coffee neighborhood, filled with third-wave coffee roasters and artisan cafés. Visit the free Kiyosumi Garden (150 JPY) — a beautiful traditional strolling garden with stepping stones across a large pond. Return to Tsukiji (10-min walk) for a final afternoon in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening splurge dinner at a mid-range sushi restaurant in Tsukiji — try Sushi Zanmai, one of the most famous affordable sushi chains, open 24 hours. Take a final evening walk along the Sumida River waterfront and Hamarikyu Gardens outer path to reflect on the trip. Pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final morning market breakfast, fresh tuna don or grilled oysters (~700–1,000 JPY)
meals.lunch: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa — specialty coffee and a sandwich or pastry at a local roastery (~600–800 JPY)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji — Sushi Zanmai omakase set or à la carte sushi (~1,500–2,000 JPY as a farewell splurge)

day_by_day.notes: The Edo-Tokyo Museum may have temporary closures — check their website. Kiyosumi-Shirakawa's coffee scene is a fascinating intersection of Tokyo's tech-savvy precision and artisan culture. Sushi Zanmai is open 24 hours and very popular with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for breakfast. Buy any last-minute food souvenirs: packaged dashi, wasabi, nori, or Japanese snacks. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the front desk or a coin locker at Tsukiji Station (300–500 JPY).
day_by_day.afternoon: Light final afternoon depending on departure time. If time permits, take a short walk to Ginza (10 min walk from Tsukiji) for any last-minute shopping at the 100-yen shops (Daiso in Ginza) or a final browse of the Itoya stationery flagship store. Head to the airport via limousine bus or train from Shimbashi or Tokyo Station.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo. Reflect on 13 days of local food, tech culture, and deep cultural immersion across one of the world's most fascinating cities.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final fresh market breakfast (~600–800 JPY)
meals.lunch: Airport or convenience store bento (~600–900 JPY)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transit. Narita Airport takes 60–90 min by train; Haneda takes 30–40 min. Refund your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for remaining balance minus a 220 JPY handling fee. Coin lockers are available at most major stations for luggage storage on the final day.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to your boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market (築地場外市場) to get your bearings. Browse fresh seafood snacks, tamagoyaki egg stalls, and local vendors. Pick up a light snack to tide you over — try grilled scallops or fresh tuna nigiri from a market stall.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (浜離宮恩賜庭園) for a peaceful evening stroll along the waterfront and tidal pond — a beautiful contrast to the urban skyline. Then head back for dinner in the Tsukiji neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market snacks — fresh nigiri, tamagoyaki, and grilled seafood skewers (budget ~¥1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai (すしざんまい) on Harumi-dori — iconic 24-hour sushi chain beloved by locals, excellent value for quality tuna sets (budget ~¥2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may kick in — keep Day 1 light and relaxed. Avoid heavy activities. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — expect beautiful scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its freshest (7:00–9:00 AM). Enjoy a proper breakfast at one of the market's beloved breakfast spots — fresh sashimi bowls or a classic Japanese breakfast set. Then walk to Ginza (銀座), Tokyo's upscale shopping and cultural district, just 10 minutes away.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ginza's galleries and architecture. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (a must for design lovers) and the Sony Park or Ginza Six atrium for a taste of Tokyo's tech-meets-culture retail scene. Browse the free gallery floors of department stores like Matsuya Ginza.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome (汐留) — the futuristic media and corporate district adjacent to Ginza — for an evening walk among illuminated skyscrapers. Visit the Caretta Shiodome mall and enjoy the free illumination displays.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — try a fresh kaisendon (seafood rice bowl) at Nakaya or Tsukiji Shoro (budget ~¥1,500–2,000)
meals.lunch: Ginza area — Kyubey lunch set (splurge option) or a more affordable bento from Mitsukoshi basement food hall (depachika) (budget ~¥1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Ramen at Fuunji-style tsukemen in Shiodome area or yakitori at a local izakaya near Shimbashi Station (budget ~¥1,500–2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Ginza galleries are often free. Depachika (department store basement food halls) are a Tokyo cultural experience in themselves — don't miss them. Shimbashi is a great spot to observe Tokyo's salaryman culture at izakayas in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa (浅草) — Tokyo's most iconic traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (浅草寺) early morning before crowds build. Walk Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Explore the backstreets of Yanaka-style old Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー) — the world's tallest broadcast tower. Purchase tickets for the Tembo Deck (350m) for panoramic views of Tokyo. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base for tech gadgets, local food products, and Japanese design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Asakusa entertainment and dining district. Walk along the Sumida River promenade, especially beautiful during cherry blossom season. Enjoy a traditional tempura or eel (unagi) dinner in Asakusa.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa morning — try ningyo-yaki (small cakes) and matcha soft serve from Nakamise stalls, plus coffee from a local kissaten (budget ~¥800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Ramen or gyudon (beef bowl) near Skytree Solamachi food floor (budget ~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Tempura Daikokuya (大黒家天麩羅) in Asakusa — legendary tempura restaurant, beloved since 1887, moderate pricing (budget ~¥2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Skytree tickets: ~¥2,100 for Tembo Deck. Book online in advance to skip queues. Senso-ji is free to enter. Friday evenings in Asakusa are lively — great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara (秋葉原) — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and global epicenter of tech culture. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera. Browse retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and cutting-edge gadget boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Akihabara's tech culture — visit the Radio Kaikan building for vintage electronics and collectibles. Stop by a maid café for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience. Then walk or take a short train to Ochanomizu and Jimbocho (神保町) — Tokyo's famous book and vintage culture district.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji/Ginza area or stay in Akihabara for dinner. Explore the vibrant Saturday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (7-Eleven or Lawson near hotel) — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and hot coffee. A quintessential Tokyo experience (budget ~¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a local curry rice shop or ramen spot in the area (budget ~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba (神田やぶそば) near Akihabara — historic soba restaurant dating to 1880, excellent cold and hot soba sets (budget ~¥1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is extremely busy on Saturdays. Some streets are pedestrianized on weekend afternoons. Maid café experience costs ~¥1,000–2,000 for a drink set. Jimbocho is great for vintage manga, maps, and secondhand books.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku (原宿). Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (明治神宮) — a serene forested Shinto shrine in the heart of the city, especially beautiful on Sunday mornings when traditional ceremonies may be held. Walk the 1km forested approach path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Takeshita Street (竹下通り) for Harajuku's famous youth fashion culture and crepe shops. Then walk through Omotesando (表参道) — Tokyo's most architecturally stunning boulevard, lined with flagship stores designed by world-renowned architects. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya (渋谷) — a 10-minute walk from Omotesando. Experience the legendary Shibuya Scramble Crossing at dusk. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck on the rooftop of Scramble Square for stunning 360° sunset views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Tsukiji market — light Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten coffee shop (budget ~¥800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Harajuku — try a Harajuku crepe (Marion Crepes or Angel Heart) and a sit-down lunch at a trendy Omotesando café (budget ~¥1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — Ichiran Ramen (一蘭ラーメン) for the famous solo-booth tonkotsu ramen experience, or explore the food floors of Shibuya Hikarie (budget ~¥1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Shibuya Sky tickets: ~¥2,000 — book online. Sunday at Meiji Jingu may feature traditional wedding processions — a wonderful cultural sight. Shibuya Scramble is most impressive at night with neon lights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets digital art museum (チームラボ) — a world-leading immersive tech-meets-art experience that perfectly bridges Tokyo's tech culture and contemporary art. Book tickets well in advance as they sell out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba (お台場) — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a life-size Gundam statue), the teamLab area, and the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset over Tokyo Bay from Odaiba's waterfront. Take the Yurikamome automated driverless monorail back toward Shiodome — a scenic and uniquely Tokyo transit experience. Dinner near Shiodome or back in Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh breakfast bowl or Japanese morning set (budget ~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.lunch: Odaiba — Aqua City or DiverCity food courts offer ramen, sushi conveyor belt, and Japanese curry options (budget ~¥1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Back near Tsukiji — try a local izakaya for yakitori, edamame, and cold beer. A great way to eat like a local (budget ~¥2,000–3,000 with drinks)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets: ~¥3,200 per person — MUST book online in advance. The Yurikamome monorail offers fantastic views of the bay and is an experience itself. Odaiba is quieter on weekdays — ideal for Monday visit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (日光) — a UNESCO World Heritage site about 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Limited Express train. Visit the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine (東照宮), one of Japan's most elaborately decorated Shinto shrines, set in a cedar forest in the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple, the Sacred Bridge (Shinkyo), and walk through the forested mountain paths. In spring, cherry blossoms and mountain scenery are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back at Tsukiji by approximately 19:00–20:00. Enjoy a relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast or hotel area café before departing for Nikko (budget ~¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Nikko — Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty. Try a yuba lunch set at a restaurant near Tosho-gu (budget ~¥1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — sushi or Japanese set meal at a neighborhood restaurant (budget ~¥2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tobu Nikko Pass (2-day) costs ~¥4,780 from Asakusa — includes round-trip train and local bus access. Tosho-ji entry: ~¥1,300. Start early (depart by 7:30–8:00 AM) to maximize time in Nikko. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Nezu Museum (根津美術館) in Omotesando — a beautiful private museum of Japanese and Asian antiquities set in a stunning traditional garden. Excellent for pre-modern Japanese art, ceramics, and calligraphy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Yanaka (谷中) neighborhood — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) areas. Walk Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent craft shops, visit old temples and cemeteries, and soak in an atmosphere that feels like Tokyo from decades past.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno (上野) — visit Ameyoko Market (アメ横) for a lively evening market atmosphere with street food, clothing, and fresh produce. Great for people-watching and snacking.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka area — try a traditional Japanese breakfast at a local kissaten or pick up fresh bread from a local bakery (budget ~¥800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza — menchi katsu (fried minced meat cutlet) from a street stall, plus local snacks (budget ~¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Ueno Ameyoko area — Korean BBQ or Japanese grilled chicken izakaya, a popular local dining option around Ueno (budget ~¥2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Museum entry: ~¥1,300, closed Mondays. Yanaka is a wonderful photography location — bring your camera. Yanaka Cemetery is peaceful and beautiful during cherry blossom season. Ameyoko is busiest in the late afternoon and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum (森美術館) in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art museums with rotating world-class exhibitions, located on the 53rd floor with stunning city views included in admission.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi (六本木) — Tokyo's international arts district. Visit the National Art Center Tokyo (国立新美術館) — a stunning Kisho Kurokawa-designed building with free-entry permanent gallery space and rotating exhibitions. Walk between the Roppongi Art Triangle venues.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Roppongi's vibrant evening scene — the area transforms after dark. Visit a rooftop bar or Tokyo Tower (東京タワー) which is nearby and beautifully illuminated at night. Walk to Zojo-ji Temple (増上寺) for a dramatic nighttime view of Tokyo Tower framed against the historic gate.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Tsukiji market breakfast (budget ~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills — Mori Tower has excellent mid-range restaurant options on upper floors with city views, or explore the plaza-level cafés (budget ~¥1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Roppongi area — try a Japanese teppanyaki restaurant or a modern izakaya. Gonpachi Nishiazabu ('Kill Bill restaurant') is nearby and worth a visit for atmosphere (budget ~¥3,000–4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum entry: ~¥2,000 (includes Tokyo City View observation deck). National Art Center is free for permanent collection. Tokyo Tower observation deck: ~¥1,200. Roppongi Art Triangle (Mori + National Art Center + Suntory Museum) can be done over two days if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (江戸東京博物館) in Ryogoku — an outstanding museum covering Tokyo's history from the Edo period to modern day, with life-size reconstructions of old Tokyo streets and bridges. Essential for understanding Tokyo's cultural evolution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ryogoku (両国) — Tokyo's sumo district. Visit the Kokugikan sumo arena (exterior and the small free sumo museum inside). Walk the neighborhood to spot sumo wrestlers from local stables going about their day. Visit Eko-in Memorial and the sumo-themed shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kiyosumi-Shirakawa (清澄白河) — Tokyo's coolest emerging neighborhood, known as the 'Brooklyn of Tokyo.' Explore the thriving specialty coffee scene and art gallery district in the early evening.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area (budget ~¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Ryogoku — chankonabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot stew) at Chanko Tomoegata or similar sumo-town restaurant — a unique cultural dining experience (budget ~¥2,000–3,000)
meals.dinner: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa — a trendy café-restaurant in this artsy neighborhood. Try Allpress Espresso or a local Japanese craft beer bar for a relaxed Friday evening (budget ~¥2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Edo-Tokyo Museum entry: ~¥600. Sumo tournaments (basho) are held in January, May, and September — April is between tournaments, but the museum and neighborhood atmosphere remain excellent. Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is a 15-minute subway ride from Ryogoku.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (鎌倉) — about 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line. Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu) — a massive 13th-century bronze Buddha statue. Explore Hase-dera Temple with its beautiful hillside garden and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills connecting Kamakura's major temples. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — Kamakura's most important shrine, set along a grand processional avenue. Browse the charming Komachi Street for local snacks and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel to rest after a full day.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — light convenience store breakfast (budget ~¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a local Kamakura specialty available at many restaurants near Hase Station (budget ~¥1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — fresh sushi or a comforting noodle dish at a local restaurant (budget ~¥2,000–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: JR Pass or Suica card works for this journey. Kamakura is very popular on weekends — depart early (before 8:00 AM) to beat crowds. Great Buddha entry: ~¥300. Hase-dera entry: ~¥400. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the hiking trail.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館) in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ancient pottery, and Buddhist sculpture. The Honkan (main building) alone is worth several hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park (上野公園) — Tokyo's most famous park, home to multiple museums, Shinobazu Pond, and Ueno Zoo. In April, the park may still have late cherry blossoms. Visit Tosho-gu Shrine within the park. Then explore the Akihabara area one more time for any last tech or souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ginza for a final upscale evening stroll. Visit the Ginza Six rooftop garden (free) for city views. Treat yourself to a special farewell dinner in the Ginza or Tsukiji area.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area — traditional Japanese breakfast at a local café or hotel (budget ~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area — bento from a park vendor or a noodle shop near the museum (budget ~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — Kyubey Ginza (久兵衛) for premium Edomae sushi (splurge night, budget ~¥5,000–8,000) OR Ginza Kojyu for an omakase experience. Alternatively, a high-quality tempura kaiseki set at Ginza Tempura Shimizu (budget ~¥4,000–6,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum entry: ~¥1,000. Ueno Park is free. Consider this your cultural capstone day. The farewell dinner is a good opportunity to splurge slightly — Ginza has some of Tokyo's finest mid-to-high-end dining within walking distance of the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take one last stroll through Tsukiji Outer Market for breakfast and to pick up any last-minute food souvenirs: dried seaweed, premium dashi packs, wasabi, matcha, and Japanese kitchen knives make excellent gifts. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if afternoon/evening flight, store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker and spend remaining time in nearby Ginza or Hamarikyu Gardens. Take the Narita Express or Airport Limousine from Tokyo Station or Shimbashi (both nearby) to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the food, tech culture, history, and neighborhoods of one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — a proper kaisendon or sashimi set as a farewell meal (budget ~¥2,000–3,000)
meals.lunch: Airport terminal — Narita Airport has excellent ramen, sushi, and bento options in the departure terminal (budget ~¥1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: In-flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transit and check-in. Narita Express takes ~60 minutes from Tokyo Station. Shimbashi Station is a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Use remaining Suica card balance on convenience store purchases at the airport — the card can be kept for future Japan visits or refunded at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime merchants and discover the heart of Tokyo's culinary culture in one of the world's most famous food markets.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Time in transit, immigration, and baggage claim at Narita/Haneda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood. Browse the iconic street-food alleys, absorb the atmosphere, and pick up light snacks — tamagoyaki rolls, fresh uni on crackers, or grilled scallops from vendor stalls. Gentle jet-lag-friendly introduction to the area.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (or equivalent Michelin-starred omakase in Tsukiji/Ginza area). Experience a refined 12–15 course nigiri omakase showcasing the finest seasonal fish sourced directly from the adjacent market. Pair with premium sake selected by the chef.

meals.breakfast: Onboard flight
meals.lunch: Light bites at Tsukiji Outer Market stalls upon arrival — fresh oysters, tamagoyaki, and green tea
meals.dinner: Omakase nigiri dinner at a Michelin-recognized sushi counter in Tsukiji/Ginza (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the omakase dinner well in advance — top counters in this area fill up months ahead. Request the hotel concierge to arrange airport transfer via private car or limousine bus for a comfortable arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — an expertly guided premium experience through the bustling market lanes. Sample fresh sushi, hand-rolled tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, wagyu beef skewers, and seasonal Japanese pickles. Meet local vendors and learn the history of Tokyo's legendary market culture. Tour runs approximately 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or short taxi to Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural district. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (a design lover's paradise), browse the Ginza Six luxury mall's art installations and rooftop garden, and explore the Hermès Maison Ginza building designed by Renzo Piano. Stop into Ginza Tsutaya Books for curated Japanese art and design publications.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten or Kyubey Ginza — legendary sushi institutions steps from your hotel neighborhood. Follow dinner with a nightcap at a Ginza whisky bar such as Bar Orchard Ginza, renowned for its Japanese whisky and fruit cocktail pairings.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Tsukiji morning coffee and fresh fruit from market vendors
meals.lunch: Premium sushi set lunch at a Ginza sushi counter (excellent value compared to dinner omakase, ¥5,000–¥15,000)
meals.dinner: Legendary omakase sushi dinner in Ginza (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour is best experienced on an empty stomach — schedule it as early as 7:00–8:00 AM for the freshest products. Ginza shops typically open at 11:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Travel by taxi or subway to Asakusa (20 minutes from Tsukiji). Explore Senso-ji Temple at dawn when crowds are thinnest — walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, washi paper fans, and ningyo-yaki cakes. Hire a rickshaw (jinrikisha) for a private 45-minute guided tour of the historic Asakusa district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sumida Hokusai Museum — a stunning aluminum-clad building by Kazuyo Sejima showcasing the works of the iconic ukiyo-e master Katsushika Hokusai. Afterward, take a short walk to the Tokyo Skytree and ascend to the Tembo Galleria (450m) for panoramic views of the city. On clear spring days, distant views of Mount Fuji are possible.
day_by_day.evening: River dinner cruise on the Sumida River — board a yakatabune (traditional roofed pleasure boat) for a private or semi-private kaiseki dinner while gliding past illuminated bridges and the Tsukiji/Shiodome skyline. A uniquely Tokyo luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local Asakusa kissaten (coffee shop) or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura Asakusa — a historic institution serving crispy Edo-style tempura since 1887
meals.dinner: Yakatabune river cruise kaiseki dinner (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person, book via hotel concierge)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is accessible 24 hours — arriving before 8:00 AM avoids tour groups. The Skytree observation deck is spectacular at sunset (around 18:00 in April). Book the yakatabune cruise at least one week in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and global epicenter of tech culture, anime, and electronics. Begin with a guided premium tech culture tour exploring multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera), retro gaming arcades, component shops, and the latest robotics and gadget showrooms. Visit the Akihabara UDX building and explore cutting-edge consumer electronics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara: visit Super Potato for rare retro gaming nostalgia, then head to the Gundam Café and explore themed concept stores. Transition to nearby Kanda for a visit to the Kanda Myojin Shrine — uniquely, this ancient Shinto shrine is the official patron of IT companies and holds regular tech-blessing ceremonies. A fascinating intersection of ancient culture and modern tech.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for dinner and evening entertainment. Witness the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing from the Scramble Square observation deck (Shibuya Sky, 230m) at dusk. Dinner at a premium teppanyaki restaurant in Shibuya with A5 Wagyu beef performance cooking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and croissant at a boutique Tsukiji café
meals.lunch: Ramen at a renowned Akihabara ramen shop — try wagyu beef ramen or premium tsukemen (dipping ramen)
meals.dinner: A5 Wagyu teppanyaki dinner at Shibuya Steak House or Ukai-tei Shibuya (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is most vibrant on weekends when pedestrian zones close the main street to traffic. Shibuya Sky tickets should be pre-booked online. Allow 90 minutes travel time between Akihabara and Shibuya.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning Edo-period feudal garden directly adjacent to your Tsukiji hotel. Stroll manicured tidal ponds, pine trees, and seasonal cherry blossom remnants (late sakura or fresh greenery in mid-April). Take tea at the traditional Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse, a 300-year-old pavilion set on a pond island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Water bus from Hamarikyu to Odaiba — a futuristic man-made island in Tokyo Bay. Explore teamLab Borderless (or teamLab Planets if Borderless is still under renovation) — an immersive digital art museum that is one of the world's most visited art spaces. Spend 2–3 hours in the mesmerizing light and projection environments.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a waterfront Odaiba restaurant with Rainbow Bridge views, then return to Tsukiji by water taxi or taxi. End the evening with a cocktail at the Park Hotel Tokyo Sky Lounge or Conrad Tokyo bar, both offering dramatic bay views.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at the hotel or fresh market breakfast from Tsukiji vendors
meals.lunch: Lunch at Odaiba's Aqua City or DiverCity complex — opt for a premium ramen or soba restaurant
meals.dinner: Contemporary Japanese cuisine at a waterfront Odaiba restaurant with Rainbow Bridge panorama (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be pre-booked online — they frequently sell out weeks in advance. The water bus from Hamarikyu Pier is a scenic and convenient connection to Odaiba (35 minutes).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Imperial Palace East Gardens — the only section of the Imperial Palace grounds open to the public. Walk the historic Ninomaru Garden, ancient stone walls, and the Sannomaru Shozokan museum housing Imperial art collections. Follow with a walk across the iconic Nijubashi Bridge for classic Tokyo photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Marunouchi — Tokyo's prestigious financial and cultural district adjacent to the palace. Visit the Mitsubishi Ichigokan Museum (housed in a beautifully restored 1894 red-brick building) for its world-class art exhibitions. Browse the high-end boutiques of Marunouchi Naka-dori avenue, lined with European elms and luxury flagships.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a French-Japanese fusion kaiseki restaurant in the Marunouchi/Nihonbashi area. Afterward, explore the atmospheric Nihonbashi district — the historic heart of Edo-era Tokyo — and visit the Coredo Muromachi complex for artisan craft and sake shops.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel or a premium bakery café near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional soba restaurant in Nihonbashi — try handmade juwari (100% buckwheat) soba with seasonal tempura
meals.dinner: French-Japanese kaiseki at a Marunouchi fine dining restaurant (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Imperial Palace East Gardens are closed on Mondays and Fridays — if this is a concern, swap with Day 7's itinerary. Confirm opening hours in advance. The Marunouchi area is easily walkable from Tsukiji (20–25 minutes on foot or 10 minutes by taxi).

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved shitamachi (old downtown) neighborhoods. Stroll the Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent pottery, lacquerware, and antique shops, and visit the serene Yanaka Cemetery lined with cherry trees. Experience Tokyo as it looked before the 20th-century transformations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's largest and oldest museum, housing over 110,000 artifacts including National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties. Explore the Honkan (Japanese Gallery) and the spectacular Heiseikan for archaeological exhibits. The museum's garden hosts seasonal tea ceremonies.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ueno/Yurakucho area. Head to Yurakucho's iconic undertrack yakitori alley — a row of tiny, atmospheric charcoal-grill restaurants beneath the elevated railway — for an authentic, convivial Tokyo evening. Choose a premium counter for Binchotan-grilled wagyu skewers and cold Sapporo draft.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a Yanaka neighborhood café — try freshly baked melon pan or tamago sando
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Tokyo National Museum restaurant or a nearby Ueno park bento from a premium deli
meals.dinner: Yakitori omakase course at a premium Yurakucho counter (¥8,000–¥15,000 per person) with craft beer or sake pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Yurakucho yakitori alley is a beloved local institution that feels worlds apart from the luxury hotel experience — a deliberately contrasting and memorable evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning visit to Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku — Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine, set within a 70-hectare forested park. Participate in a private misogi (purification ritual) or simply walk the grand torii-lined approach in contemplative quiet. Visit the Treasure Museum annex for Imperial artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Omotesando — Tokyo's most architecturally significant boulevard, lined with landmark buildings by Tadao Ando (Omotesando Hills), Herzog & de Meuron (Prada Aoyama), and SANAA (Dior). Browse flagship luxury boutiques, visit the Nezu Museum for its extraordinary Japanese and East Asian art collection set in a bamboo garden, and explore the hidden backstreets of Ura-Harajuku for independent designer boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège or a comparable innovative Japanese contemporary restaurant in Aoyama — one of Tokyo's most celebrated modern French-Japanese restaurants with a theatrical open kitchen. Follow dinner with cocktails at The SG Club in Shibuya, one of Asia's top-ranked cocktail bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and pastry near Tsukiji before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium café or restaurant in Omotesando Hills — try the basement food hall for artisan Japanese sweets and light fare
meals.dinner: Innovative kaiseki or French-Japanese tasting menu at Florilège or equivalent (¥30,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays. Book Florilège or equivalent restaurant at least 2–3 months in advance. Omotesando Hills' basement food floor is an excellent spot for premium Japanese sweets and gift shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Tech culture deep dive: visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba — one of the world's finest science museums. Interact with ASIMO-style robots, explore AI and space exploration exhibits, and experience the iconic Geo-Cosmos — a 6-meter spherical display showing real-time Earth imagery from space.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sony Park in Ginza (a short ride from Odaiba) — Sony's flagship experiential space showcasing the latest audio, imaging, and entertainment technology. Continue to the Panasonic Center Tokyo or the Canon Gallery for additional tech culture immersion. End the afternoon at the Itabashi Innovation Center or explore Akihabara's specialized component and maker culture shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium Ginza restaurant. Try Ginza Kojyu (four-star kaiseki) or Quintessence (three-Michelin-star French). End the evening with a visit to a rooftop bar — try the Andaz Tokyo Toranomon Hills Sky Bar for sweeping city panoramas and Japanese-inspired cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at the hotel or a Tsukiji market morning snack run
meals.lunch: Lunch at Miraikan's in-house restaurant or a nearby Odaiba waterfront café
meals.dinner: Three or four Michelin-star kaiseki or French fine dining in Ginza (¥40,000–¥70,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. Book Ginza Kojyu or Quintessence months in advance — these are among Tokyo's most sought-after reservations. The Andaz Sky Bar has a smart-casual dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Private sake brewery tour and tasting in the Nihonbashi area — visit a historic sake wholesaler or the Hakutsuru Sake Brewery experience center. Learn about the ancient craft of nihonshu production, the role of koji mold, seasonal brewing, and regional terroir. Guided premium tasting of 6–8 curated sakes from across Japan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nihonbashi Takashimaya department store — a national cultural property building and Japan's most prestigious department store. Browse the basement food hall (depachika), one of the finest in the world, for wagyu beef, artisan confections, premium teas, and curated Japanese products. Visit the rooftop garden and the art gallery floors.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at Narisawa — consistently ranked among the world's 50 best restaurants, chef Yoshihiro Narisawa's 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' celebrates Japan's forests, mountains, and coastlines through extraordinary tasting menus. A once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Tsukiji morning market snacks
meals.lunch: Premium bento or artisan sushi from the Nihonbashi Takashimaya depachika food hall, enjoyed in a nearby garden
meals.dinner: Narisawa Innovative Satoyama Cuisine tasting menu (¥45,000–¥65,000 per person, wine pairing available)

day_by_day.notes: Narisawa reservations must be made months in advance via their website — this is one of Tokyo's most exclusive tables. The Nihonbashi sake tour can be arranged through the hotel concierge or a specialist food tour company.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours by Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the mountains north of Tokyo. Explore the extraordinarily ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, with its famous 'hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil' monkeys and the Yomeimon Gate covered in over 500 intricate carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: visit Rinno-ji Temple and the serene Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. Walk through cryptomeria cedar forests to the quieter Futarasan Shrine. Enjoy the mountain air and lush spring greenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relaxed dinner close to the hotel in Tsukiji — a premium kappo (counter-style traditional Japanese) restaurant for a more intimate, low-key evening after a full day of travel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Asakusa
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) kaiseki lunch in Nikko — a regional specialty using pure mountain spring water
meals.dinner: Kappo-style Japanese dinner near Tsukiji (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person)

day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner: reserve a table at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Ebisu) — the legendary three-Michelin-star French restaurant in a château-style mansion.
